title: people-ops-partner-rubric-and-90-day-reboarding-experiment
summary: Working draft: combined interview rubric for People Ops Partner candidates plus a structured 90-day reboarding experiment for lateral hires and internal transfers. Focus on operational rigor, stakeholder influence, and inclusive hiring signals. Intended to reduce variability across interviewers and speed up early impact for hires coming from contracting or internal moves.
purpose: Create a repeatable, low-noise evaluation for People Ops Partner candidates and a parallel reboarding playbook to validate early retention/impact hypotheses for hires transitioning into the role.
audience: Hiring managers for People Ops, interview panel members, recruiting partners, onboarding leads, people-ops-sre partners.
hiring_goals: Fill 2 People Ops Partner roles Q4 2025 (one US, one EU)
Target time-to-offer: 18 days from first screen
Diversity goal: shortlist at least 50% underrepresented candidates per opening
interview_rubric_description: Compact, behavioral + work-sample focused rubric. Score 1-4 for five dimensions. Interviewers should annotate specific examples and map to a suggested hire/no-hire threshold. Use the rubric for calibration sessions before panel interviews.
rubric_dimensions: 1) Operational Excellence (scale, process): Score considers evidence of running end-to-end programs, SLOs, measurements, and follow-up. 1=no repeatable delivery, 4=owned multiple org-scale programs with clear SLOs and auditable outcomes.

2) Stakeholder Influence (cross-functional): Score considers examples of influencing engineers, product, legal, and finance. 1=limited stakeholder reach, 4=proven ability to shift cross-functional roadmaps and secure resources.

3) Program Design & Metrics: Score looks for ability to convert business problems into measurable people programs (e.g., onboarding funnel, Attrition-by-cohort metric). 1=ambiguous success metrics, 4=defined metrics and instrumentation plans.

4) Inclusion & Psychological Safety: Score evaluates concrete practices (inclusive hiring panels, equitable interview design, remediation paths). 1=little to no inclusive practice, 4=designed and iterated programs that improved representation or belonging metrics.

5) Communication & Facilitation: Score assesses ability to run cross-org syncs, write clear decision memos, and surface risks. 1=unclear communication, 4=regular facilitation of org-level decisions and concise memos used by execs.

Scoring anchors (one-line): 1=insufficient / risk; 2=basic competency; 3=strong contributor; 4=exceptional / scale leader. Recommended minimum passing score across all dimensions: average >=2.75 and no dimension <2.

Panel guidance: Screeners focus on 'operational excellence' and 'communication'; onsite panel should include a scenario exercise (45min) that requires candidate to design a 90-day reboarding experiment for a transfer hire, including metrics and stakeholder map. Interviewers capture verbatim candidate phrasing for calibration.

Calibration note: Run a 60min calibration with 6 mock evaluations for each open role; ensure variance in scores under 0.7 standard deviation before progressing to offers. Document outliers and vote rationale in JIRA ticket.

Work-sample prompt (to give candidates ahead of interview): 'Design a 90-day reboarding plan for a senior IC moving into People Ops Partner. Include success metrics, checkpoints, and remediation triggers. You will present for 10 minutes and take 15 minutes of questions.'
scoring_sheet_example: Overall recommendation: Hire | No Hire | Hire with Conditions
Optional notes for recruiter: ramp needs, visa constraints, compensation band suggestions
90_day_reboarding_experiment_overview: Experiment: 'Fast-Embed Reboarding' - structured cohort of 3 transfers/contractors hired into People Ops Partner with intensive 1:1 and outcome-driven checkpoints. Goal: increase 90-day time-to-impact and reduce early attrition for non-traditional hires.
hypotheses: H1: Structured reboarding with a 1:6 mentor ratio and weekly decision memos reduces time-to-first-impact from 60 to 30 days.
H2: Explicitly documented remediation triggers at day 14 and day 30 reduce ambiguity and increase retention at 90 days by 12%.
H3: Work-sample alignment (candidate designing their reboarding plan during interview) correlates with higher early performance ratings.
H4: Pairing transfers with a single engineering partner during weeks 1-4 improves cross-functional signal quality and reduces context switching cost.
experimental_cohort_structure: Pre-day0: hiring manager + mentor prepare a 2-pager with context, key stakeholders, and a list of 6 priority tickets/projects.
Day0: Welcome sync (45min) with manager, mentor, and onboarding coordinator; hardware/software check; first 1:1 scheduled.
Week1 (days 1-7): 5 x 30min shadow sessions with stakeholders, 2 kickoff tasks with clear acceptance criteria, first decision memo due at day 7.
Week2-4: Focused mini-sprints (3 deliverables) with weekly syncs; day-14 remediation checkpoint using explicit rubric (go/no-go/support plan).
Week5-8: Ownership on one program with mentor review; instrumentation of at least one metric; peer feedback collection at week 8.
Week9-12: Transition to normal cadence; handoff doc and 'lessons learned' doc for the cohort; performance check at day 90.
success_metrics: Time-to-first-impact (goal: <= 30 days measured by accepted deliverable with stakeholder sign-off)
Retention at 90 days (goal: >= 95% for cohort vs baseline 83%)
Stakeholder satisfaction (survey net promoter-style question; goal >= 4/5 average)
Ramp quality: % of assigned tickets accepted without rework (goal >= 80%)
onboarding_checklist: Preboarding (recruiter): send role context doc and stakeholder list; ensure permissions reqs are submitted 7 days before start.
Day0: Set up accounts, intro to people-ops playbooks, send cohort calendar and expectations memo.
Week1 tasks: complete shadow schedule, join two recurring stakeholder meetings as observer, deliver first small-ticket and submit decision memo.
Week2 tasks: complete partner interviews (structured 30min each) to gather context; present a 10-min plan for first program at week2 sync.
Week4 check: mentor + manager evaluate against remediation rubric; if any dimension <2, deploy 14-day support plan.
Week8 deliverable: ownable program with instrumentation and dashboard stub; collect peer feedback.
Day90 wrap: performance review + cohort retrospective; capture changes to playbook and publish to Confluence.
remediation_triggers_and_playbook: Trigger A (day 14): missed first deliverable or unclear acceptance criteria -> Action: 2-week focused support, paired tasks, daily standups with mentor.
Trigger B (day 30): stakeholder dissatisfaction on metric or failure to produce measurable progress -> Action: escalate to hiring manager, set 30-day corrective plan with clear exit criteria.
Trigger C (day 60): ongoing performance gaps -> schedule HR-career conversation, consider role reshaping or redeployment options.
data_collection_plan: Weekly pulse survey (3 questions) for stakeholders and new hire
Instrumented deliverable tracking in JIRA with 'accepted-by' custom field
Mentor weekly note template stored in Confluence; anonymized for analysis
90-day retrospective captured as a short doc and a 10-slide deck for exec summary
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Mentor overload -> Mitigation: cap mentor at 3 active reboards and use 'mentor office hours' model.
Risk: Variability in hiring panel scoring -> Mitigation: mandatory calibration and calibration checklist; exclude interviews from decision if calibration not attended.
Risk: Failure to instrument metrics -> Mitigation: default JIRA fields required in offer packet and onboarding checklist.
notes_to_reviewers: Please focus feedback on: 1) pass/fail thresholds in rubric, 2) feasibility of mentor ratios for Q4 hiring plan, 3) clarity of remediation triggers. If you volunteer to host a calibration session, add your name to the linked slack thread.
